newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum sees no negative impact from 30-year bond.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum sees no negative impact from 30-year bond.

text.p: Bundesbank deputy president Johann Gaddum said on Tuesday that he did not expect the issue of a new 30-year government bond to have a negative impact on the German debt market by removing expectations of further interest rate cuts.
Asked if he feared that financial markets would interpret the 30-year issue as a sign that Germany's rate cutting cycle had come to an end, Gaddum said: "No".
"I believe we have a relatively stable capital market situation at the moment. I do not expect a negative impact effect in this direction," he said.
Gaddum noted that previous 30-year bond issues in Germany had coincided with interest rate lows, but said conditions were different now.
Gaddum was speaking at a news conference called to announce the issuance of a new strippable 30-year bond.
